question.text: A rod <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>AB</mi></math> of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi></math> and length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">L</mi></math> is lying on a horizontal frictionless surface. A particle of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> travelling along the surface hits the end <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> of the rod with a velocity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">v</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></math> in a direction perpendicular to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>AB</mi></math>. The collision is perfectly elastic and after the collision, the particle comes to rest. The ratio <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi></mfrac></math> is

solution.text:
Using the principle of conservation of linear momentum

mv0=Mvcm

Using the principle of conservation of angular momentum

mv0L2=ML212ω

Since the collision is completely elastic, the velocity of approach is equal to the velocity of separation

v0=vcm+ωL2

⇒v0=mMv0+3mMv0

⇒mM=14
